auto.title: Seal automatically
auto.description: When everyone you are writing to can receive sealed mail, Owlat encrypts the message before it leaves. Recommended.

ask.title: Keep available, but never automatic
ask.description: Owlat keeps discovering keys and shows when a message could be sealed, but never seals on its own — messages are sent normally. Switch to "Seal automatically" to turn on sealing.

off.title: Never seal
off.description: All Postbox mail is sent normally, even when a recipient could receive it sealed.

toasts.noKeyForAddress: No sealed-mail key exists for that address yet.
toasts.kitDownloaded: Recovery kit downloaded. Store it somewhere private and offline.
toasts.kitImported: Recovery kit imported. Sealed mail for this address can be opened again.
toasts.kitMismatch: That key doesn't match this address, so it wasn't imported.
toasts.reSealStarted: Re-sealing started. Once it finishes you can remove the previous instance secret.

sealedMail.title: Sealed Mail
sealedMail.intro: How Owlat encrypts personal mail between you and other Owlat workspaces.
sealedMail.noWorkspace: Select a workspace to manage its sealing policy.
sealedMail.disabledNotice: Sealed Mail is turned off for this workspace, so nothing is sealed yet. You can still choose the policy below — it takes effect once Sealed Mail is enabled in Features.

tls.title: Require TLS for incoming mail
tls.description: Reject senders that try to deliver without STARTTLS. They receive a permanent “550 5.7.10 Encryption needed” response, so the message is never accepted or stored.
tls.plaintextWarning: Plaintext inbound delivery is allowed. Only disable this for legacy mail servers that cannot use TLS.

recoveryKit.title: Recovery kit
recoveryKit.description: A recovery kit is the private key that opens sealed mail for one address, plus plain-language instructions. Download one for each address and keep it somewhere private and offline. There is no master copy on the server, so a recovery kit is the only way to restore sealed mail if this instance is rebuilt.
recoveryKit.restoreDescription: Paste a previously downloaded recovery kit to restore access for its address.
recoveryKit.importKeyPlaceholder: Paste the ASCII-armored private key from your recovery kit

reSeal.title: After changing the instance secret
reSeal.description: If you rotate this instance's secret, keep the previous one in place until you run this. Re-sealing re-encrypts every stored key under the new secret so the old one can be retired. Sealed mail keeps opening throughout.

index.title: Plugins
index.intro: Configure each installed plugin. Enabling a plugin and approving the capabilities it requests happens under {featuresLink}; this page manages each plugin's own settings.

empty.title: No plugins installed
empty.description: Bundled plugins are added to this deployment's build. Once a plugin is installed it appears here to configure.

residual.title: Residual settings
residual.description: These plugins are no longer installed. Their stored settings can be cleared.

confirm.title: Clear settings for {pluginId}?
confirm.description: This permanently removes the stored settings for this uninstalled plugin, including any saved secrets.

orphaned.title: {pluginId} is no longer installed
orphaned.description: This plugin was removed from the build but left stored settings behind. Clear them to remove any saved values, including secrets.

notFound.title: Plugin not found
notFound.description: No installed plugin matches this address.

detail.disabledNotice: This plugin is disabled. You can configure its settings now; enable it and approve its capabilities under {featuresLink}.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.description: Host-mediated operations this plugin declared, and whether the operator has granted each.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Configuration this plugin exposes. Secrets are supplied by deployment environment variables, never stored by Owlat.
settings.none: This plugin has no configurable settings.
settings.envVarsNotice: This plugin needs an environment variable set in your deployment before it can run. Other settings can still be saved. | This plugin needs environment variables set in your deployment before it can run. Other settings can still be saved.

resetConfirm.title: Reset plugin settings?
resetConfirm.description: This clears every stored value for this plugin, including saved secrets, and returns it to the schema defaults.

orphanClearConfirm.title: Clear residual settings?
orphanClearConfirm.description: This permanently removes the stored settings this uninstalled plugin left behind, including any saved secrets. This cannot be undone.

index.title: API Keys
index.subtitle: Manage API keys for authenticating your API requests

secureNotice.title: Keep your API keys secure
secureNotice.body: API keys grant full access to your account via the API. Never share your keys publicly or commit them to version control. Use environment variables to store your keys securely.

rateLimit.title: Rate Limiting
rateLimit.rateDescription: Maximum API calls per second per API key
rateLimit.resetHeader: Unix timestamp when the rate limit resets
rateLimit.retryAfterHeader: Seconds to wait when rate limited (429 response)

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.description: View endpoint reference, request schemas, and code examples

adminGate.title: Admins only
adminGate.description: API keys can only be managed by workspace owners and admins. Ask an admin if you need API access.

noWorkspace.title: No workspace selected
noWorkspace.description: Create or select a workspace to manage API keys.

empty.title: No API keys yet
empty.description: Create an API key to start using the API for contacts, emails, and events.

form.nameHelp: Give your API key a descriptive name to identify its purpose.
form.scopesHelp: Grant only the permissions this key needs. A compromised key can do nothing beyond its scopes.

created.title: API Key Created
created.copyNowBody: This is the only time you'll see this key. Store it securely - you won't be able to see it again.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke API Key
revokeDialog.description: Revoking "{name}" will immediately disable the key. Any API requests using this key will fail. You can delete the key later to remove it completely.

deleteDialog.title: Delete API Key
deleteDialog.description: Permanently delete "{name}"? This action cannot be undone. The key will be permanently removed from your account.

index.title: Connected apps
index.intro: External apps that talk to Owlat through a scoped, plugin-bound secret and signed hooks. A connected app can add work or caution — it can never approve, unblock, or send for you.

adminGate.title: Admins only
adminGate.description: Connected apps can be managed by workspace owners and admins. Ask an admin if you need to connect an external app.

empty.title: No connected apps
empty.description: Connect an external app to extend Owlat with scoped access and signed hooks.

rotateDialog.title: Rotate the secret for {name}?
rotateDialog.description: A new shared secret is generated and shown once. The current secret stops working immediately — the connected app will fail until you update it with the new secret.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke {name}?
revokeDialog.description: Revoking is permanent. The shared secret is invalidated, the app can no longer call Owlat, and it can never be re-enabled — you'd have to connect a new app. Its record is kept for audit until you delete it.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {name}?
deleteDialog.description: This permanently removes the connected app and its record. This cannot be undone.

reconnectPanel.title: Reconnect this inbox

deleteDialog.description: Delete "{name}"? Its synced mail, the member roster, and the stored mailbox connection are erased for everyone. This cannot be undone.
